liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Funiculi Funicula** (2 other sources): This tuning jam occurs before Me And My Uncle; Tuning was heard before Me And My Uncle [3][5]
- **Tons Of Steel** (1 review, 1 other source): Reviewer considers this one of the better versions heard; Brent sings a line hoping his bass player will cut him some slack [5][14]
- **Sugar Magnolia** (1 review): Reviewer notes the show opened with this song, questions when it last did, and finds the band still warming up [14]
- **Sugaree** (1 review): Reviewer singles out Weir's guitar playing on this song as outstanding [9]
- **Let It Grow** (1 review): Reviewer singles out Lesh's bass playing on this song [9]

## The recordings

- **gd1987-05-09.165064.UltraMatrix.sbd.cm.miller.t-flac1644** (recommended): soundboard; 21 songs; 149 min [1]
- **gd1987-05-09.163534.ultramatrix.miller.flac2496**: soundboard; 21 songs; 149 min [2]
- **gd1987-05-09.167185.neumann.km84i.hecht.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 20 songs; 144 min [3]
- **gd1987-05-09.sbd.walker-scotton.miller.83749.sbeok.flac16**: soundboard; 21 songs; 139 min; rated 4.17/5 by 6 [6]. Said about its sound: Reviewer says this recording feels like the live event and sounds better than the Oade Bros. version [19]
- **gd87-05-09.sbd.cole.5059.sbeok.shnf**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 19 songs; 137 min; rated 3.67/5 by 12 [8]

## Around the show

- The Touch of Grey video was shot at midnight between shows; people rushed there expecting a free show [10]
- Reviewer jumped the fence with new friends and was chased uphill by people on ATVs [11]
- Reviewer was 17 and lived about two miles from the venue [12]
- Weather was great with roughly 50,000 people camping; calamari was sold, and the ground near the stage felt like it moved [13]
- The Touch of Grey video filming ran long, finishing around 5:00 a.m [13]
- Ry Cooder opened, and Hornsby also played, performing his own take on I Know You Rider [15]
- Reviewer recalls the bouncy ground on the left side of the stage, like walking on a blister [15]
- Reviewer also remembers the squishy ground at the show [16]
- Reviewer finds the setlist ordinary, especially after Space, apart from the Iko Iko encore [9]
- Reviewer recalls the next night's show as stronger, with a very hot four-song opening, and Weir's licks on Stranger [10]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1987-05-09.165064.UltraMatrix.sbd.cm.miller.t-flac1644**: taped by Recorded by Don Pearson and Dan Healy; transferred by All Transfers and Mastering by Charlie Miller  February 2, 2023; source: Ultramatrix SBD > Cassette Master (TDK MA-XG) [1]. Also: Recorded by Don Pearson and Dan Healy; several masters were combined to complete the show [1]
- **gd1987-05-09.163534.ultramatrix.miller.flac2496**: taped by Recorded by Don Pearson and Dan Healy; transferred by All Transfers and Mastering by Charlie Miller  February 2, 2023; source: Ultramatrix SBD > Cassette Master (TDK MA-XG) [2]. Also: Recorded by Don Pearson and Dan Healy, with multiple masters used to make the show complete [2]
- **gd1987-05-09.167185.neumann.km84i.hecht.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Chris Hecht; transferred by Scott Clugston, Charlie Miller; source: Chris Hecht's Master Audience Cassettes; Neumann KM84i mics > Sony D5M [3]. Also: A Sennheiser 2002 source supplies a 4:47 patch in Drums [3]
- **gd1987-05-09.sbd.walker-scotton.miller.83749.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Cassette Master (Maxell MX90/Sony D5) [6]
- **gd87-05-09.sbd.cole.5059.sbeok.shnf**: source: SBD (matrix)> PCM> Dat [8]. Also: Reviewer says high-quality tapes were recorded in front of the soundboard, with equipment smuggled in by the reviewer's group [16]

## Art and photos

- Fan art by www.gdao.org: [-- Eimon · Grateful Dead Archive Online · Grateful Dead Archive Online](https://www.gdao.org/items/show/811528) [22]
